rows.jp: でも部活があるしな。
rows.en: But I had club work to do.

ghs.en: But I have club don't I.
ghs.assessment: The club activity requires a determiner or complement, and the tag question requires punctuation.

rows.jp: 先輩の図面。
rows.en: Mimi’s plans.

ghs.assessment: The Japanese status title is left unexplained rather than represented in English.

rows.jp: この泣き言リストが問題点だとして、これを解決すれば発信できる体制になると信じよう。
rows.en: Assuming this list of gripes really did cover every problem, I had to believe that solving them would leave us ready to transmit.

ghs.en: This sob-filled list of complaints is the problem at hand, and I want to believe that if these points are resolved, the system will become capable of signal transmission.

rows.jp: 先輩を信じるのだ。
rows.en: I had to believe in her.

ghs.assessment: The narrator exhorts himself to trust his senior. The English instead makes the senior the person who believes something and leaves the title untranslated.

rows.jp: 信じる。美しい言葉である。
rows.en: Believe. What a beautiful word.

ghs.en: Believe. What a beautiful word that is.

rows.jp: 乾きを潤してあまりある。
rows.en: Enough to quench even the deepest thirst.

ghs.en: There is so much there to dampen the dryness, to quench a thirst.

rows.jp: 作業開始。
rows.en: I began.

rows.jp: 炎天下での作業が続く。
rows.en: The work continued beneath the punishing sun.

ghs.en: Fatigue duty continues under the scorching sun.
ghs.assessment: This is continued work under the blazing sun. 'Fatigue duty' specifically denotes noncombat manual labor assigned to soldiers, often as routine or punishment, which the source does not establish.

rows.jp: 俺は日射には滅法強い。
rows.en: I could take direct sunlight like nobody's business.

ghs.en: I am extraordinarily resistant to sunstroke,
ghs.assessment: 日射 means solar radiation or exposure to sunlight. 'Sunstroke' is a medical condition, not the environmental stimulus to which his white hair supposedly makes him resistant.

rows.jp: 髪が白いからだ。
rows.en: It was the white hair.

rows.jp: これだけでかなり違ってくる。
rows.en: That alone made a world of difference.

ghs.en: That alone makes quite the difference.

rows.jp: そんなわけで真夏日だが、作業は進む。
rows.en: And so, midsummer heat or not, the work went on.

ghs.en: Today may be a Manatsubi, with its temperature likely above 30 Celsius, but work continues.
ghs.assessment: 真夏日 is a hot summer day, technically one reaching thirty degrees Celsius. The English leaves the term romanized and inserts an explanatory aside into the prose instead of rendering it.

highlights.text: a Manatsubi, with its temperature likely above 30 Celsius

rows.jp: ほどなくして。
rows.en: Before long—

rows.jp: 霧じゃないか。
rows.en: Wasn’t that Kiri?

rows.jp: フェンスの際に立って、景色を眺めている。
rows.en: She stood by the fence, gazing at the view.

ghs.en: Standing at the edge of the fence, gazing at the landscape.

rows.jp: 俺に気づいてないのか。
rows.en: Had she not noticed me?

rows.jp: そんなはずはない。大きな音を立てて作業しているのだから。
rows.en: Not a chance. I was making a hell of a racket.

ghs.en: That can't be. I'm making very loud noises working here.

rows.jp: 「おーい、霧ー！」
rows.en: “Heeey, Kiri!”

rows.jp: 呼ぶと。
rows.en: At my call—

rows.jp: 霧はゆったりとした歩調で歩いてきた。
rows.en: Kiri sauntered over.

ghs.en: Kiri walked to me at a loose, easy pace.

rows.jp: 「なんですか」
rows.en: “What is it?”

rows.jp: 「いや……特に用事ってわけじゃ……」
rows.en: “Nothing... It's not like I needed anything...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Well... it's not like I have anything in particular in mind..."

rows.jp: 霧はちらと興味なさげにアンテナを見あげた。
rows.en: Kiri cast the antenna one indifferent glance.

ghs.en: Kiri glanced, seemingly disinterested, up at the antenna.

rows.jp: 「……部活、本当にやってるんですね」
rows.en: “...You really are doing club work.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "...you are really doing this club thing then."

rows.jp: 「まあな」
rows.en: “More or less.”

rows.jp: 「こう暑いと、海にでも行きたくなるけど」
rows.en: “Weather like this makes me want to go to the beach.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But with this heat I actually wanted to go to the beach."
ghs.assessment: He says the current heat makes him want to go to the beach. The past tense moves the desire out of the present conversation.

rows.jp: 「去年は行ったよな。覚えてるか？」
rows.en: “We went last year, remember?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "We went last year. Remember that?"

rows.jp: 「楽しかったな。美希には悪いけど」
rows.en: “That was fun. Though I do feel bad for Miki.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "That was so fun! Too bad about Miki, though."
ghs.assessment: Taichi says he feels bad for Miki while recalling that it was fun. 'Too bad about Miki' sounds dismissive and can mean her misfortune is merely unfortunate.

rows.jp: やけに素直だな。
rows.en: That was awfully compliant of her.

rows.jp: というか様子が変だ。
rows.en: No—she was acting strange.

ghs.en: Or should I say, things are weird.

rows.en: “...What's wrong?”

rows.jp: 「その……支倉先輩が……」
rows.en: “Um... Hasekura...”

ghs.assessment: The surname-plus-status address is left in Japanese morphology rather than represented in English.

rows.jp: 「曜子ちゃんが……監視してる？」
rows.en: “Youko is... watching you?”

ghs.assessment: The affectionate Japanese suffix remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

rows.en: “Y-yes...”

rows.jp: 霧の手が震えている。
rows.en: Kiri’s hands were trembling.

rows.jp: あんなに気丈な娘だったのに。
rows.en: She used to be so strong.

ghs.en: despite her being so stout-hearted a girl.

rows.jp: 怯えて。
rows.en: Now she was terrified.

rows.jp: 見る影もなく、萎縮していた。
rows.en: She was a shadow of herself, utterly cowed.

rows.jp: 「それで」
「それで……」
rows.en: “And so...”

rows.jp: 声が震える。
rows.en: Her voice shook.

ghs.assessment: Kiri's voice trembles. The English omits both the possessor and the article required for a count noun.

rows.jp: 見ていられなかった。
rows.en: I could not bear to watch.

rows.jp: 未成熟ながら、美しいガラス細工みたいな女の子だったのに。
rows.en: She was still unfinished, but beautiful—like a work of glass.

ghs.en: Because she was immature an immature girl, and yet so like a beautiful glass sculpture.
ghs.assessment: The adjective and noun phrase are accidentally duplicated around a missing conjunction or comma.

highlights.text: she was immature an immature girl

rows.jp: 触れれば汚れ、掴めば壊れてしまいそうな脆さがあったのに。
rows.en: So fragile that a touch might smudge her, a grip might shatter her.

ghs.en: Because she had this fragility, that to touch was to make her filthy, and to grip was to shatter her.

rows.jp: こんな……中途半端な有様は、どういうことだ。
rows.en: How had she been left so... incomplete?

ghs.en: But what to do with something this... half-baked.
ghs.assessment: The narrator asks how Kiri came to be left in this damaged, incomplete state. The English turns her into an object he must decide what to do with and uses 'half-baked,' which means poorly planned.

highlights.text: what to do with something this... half-baked

rows.jp: 曜子ちゃんを恨む気持ちがある。
rows.en: Part of me hated Youko for it.

ghs.assessment: The affectionate Japanese suffix remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

rows.jp: ああ、俺はまた沈んでいるなと思う。
rows.en: And then I knew: I was sinking again.

ghs.en: Ahhh, don't sink down again, you.
ghs.assessment: The narrator observes that he himself is sinking again emotionally. The English converts that realization into a second-person command not to sink.

rows.jp: テンション高めに保っていられる時はいい。
rows.en: As long as I could keep myself revved up, I was fine.

ghs.en: I prefer times where the tension can be kept high.
ghs.assessment: テンション here means his energy, spirits, or excited mood. The English false friend 'tension' suggests stress or strain and changes the psychological state.

highlights.text: the tension can be kept high

rows.jp: そうでない時、俺の心は沈んでいく。
rows.en: The moment I couldn't, I began to sink.

ghs.en: In times where it can't, my heart sinks.
ghs.assessment: When he cannot keep his spirits high, his heart sinks. The English uses the false friend 'tension,' assigns ability to an unexplained 'it,' and uses 'where' for time.

rows.jp: 深い部分。
rows.en: Into the depths.

rows.jp: 日が届かない深淵。
rows.en: An abyss the sun never reached.

ghs.en: An abyss that sunlight doesn't reach.

rows.jp: 光のあたたかさを忘れさせ、ただ個体で生きるものにする場所。
rows.en: A place that made you forget the warmth of light and reduced you to an organism living alone.

ghs.en: A place that makes you forget all the light, that swallows whole all that desires but to live as an Individual.
ghs.assessment: The abyss makes him forget the warmth of light and reduces a being to living as a mere isolated organism. The English omits warmth, introduces a consuming entity, and changes the organism into 'all that desires' to live.

highlights.text: A place that makes you forget all the light, that swallows whole all that desires but to live as an Individual.

rows.jp: 心というものが必要ない場所。
rows.en: A place where no heart was required.

ghs.en: A place where this thing called a heart is unnecessary.

rows.jp: 長くいれば、凍った心もやがて退化し、純粋な生きる意志。
rows.en: Stay there long enough and even the frozen heart would atrophy, until all that remained was the pure will to live.

ghs.en: Being there for long eventually makes this frozen heart degenerate into a pure volition to live.
ghs.assessment: After long enough, even the frozen heart atrophies, leaving only a pure will to live. The English says the heart itself transforms into that will, changing subtraction into metamorphosis.

highlights.text: makes this frozen heart degenerate into a pure volition to live

rows.jp: 自分が深海に生きる存在であるように錯覚する。
rows.en: You began to mistake yourself for some creature born to the deep.

ghs.en: There's this hallucination that I am as if something that lives deep beneath the seas.

rows.jp: それもいいと思うのだ。
rows.en: And part of me thought that might be good.

ghs.en: That, I think, would also be good.

rows.jp: たとえば世界に、自分一人だけならば。
rows.en: If I were the only person left in the world, for instance.

ghs.en: For example, if I were to be by myself in this world alone,

rows.jp: 傷つけないで済むから。
rows.en: Then there'd be no one left for me to hurt.

ghs.en: I would have no need to hurt anyone.

rows.jp: 「……霧、部活手伝え」
rows.en: “...Kiri. Help me with the club work.”

rows.jp: 唐突な提案は、霧の瞳を円形にした。
rows.en: Kiri's eyes went round at the sudden suggestion.

ghs.en: The sudden proposal made Kiri's pupils turn circular.

rows.jp: 「ぶかつ？」
rows.en: “Club work?”

rows.jp: 「そうだ」
rows.en: “Yes.”

rows.jp: 「……一人では……終わらんのだ……助けてくれ……」
rows.en: “...I-I’ll never... finish alone... Please help me...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...alone I... can't finish this and... help me please..."

rows.jp: 先輩から引き継いだ泣き言を、下級生にそのままぶつけた。
rows.en: I took the whole litany of complaints Mimi had handed down to me and handed it straight down to my underclassman.

ghs.en: I thrust, unaltered, the complaints I inherited from a Senpai onto an underclassman.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese status title remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

rows.jp: 霧に脚立の上で作業させることによって、パンチランド建国という幸運も期待している自分がいた。
rows.en: Some part of me was also looking forward to the glorious founding of Pantyland once I put Kiri to work atop a stepladder.

ghs.en: Because there also exist the expectation within myself that via making Kiri work on top of the stepladder the blessed event that is the Foundation of Panchiraland will occur.
ghs.assessment: The clause has singular 'expectation' with plural agreement and wraps the narrator's private hope in an unnatural existential-locative construction.

highlights.text: there also exist the expectation within myself

rows.jp: 「パンチラはいい……」
rows.en: “Panty shots are—”

ghs.assessment: パンチラ means a glimpse of underwear and is directly relevant to the coined 'Panchiraland' joke. Leaving it romanized makes the joke inaccessible in English.

rows.jp: 「今、なんて言いました？」
rows.en: “What did you just say?”

ghs.en: Kiri: "What... did you just say right then?"

rows.jp: 「アンテナがＥ型という機種でな」
rows.en: “The antenna's an E-type. That's what I said.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "The antenna is an E-plane type, you know."

rows.jp: 「パンチラと聞こえたのですけど」
rows.en: “I distinctly heard ‘panty shots.’”

ghs.assessment: Kiri explicitly says she heard the word for a glimpse of underwear. The untranslated romanization withholds the content of her accusation.

rows.jp: 「言ってないよそんなこと」
rows.en: “I said nothing of the kind.”

ghs.assessment: He denies the just-completed utterance: 'I didn't say that.' Present perfect is unnatural with this specific immediate past event.

rows.jp: 口笛を吹く。
rows.en: I whistled.

rows.jp: 「……何、したらいいんですか？」
rows.en: “...What do you want me to do?”

rows.jp: 「手伝ってくれるの？」
rows.en: “You’ll help?”

rows.jp: 「命令なんですよね？」
rows.en: “It’s an order, isn’t it?”

rows.jp: 「……あー、まー、そーねー」
rows.en: “...Uh. Yeah. Let's call it that.”

rows.jp: 「借りは返しきっておきたいですし、手伝います」
rows.en: “I want to settle what I owe you once and for all. So I'll help.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "As I want to return what I borrowed in full, I will help."
ghs.assessment: 借り refers to an obligation or favor owed, not a physical borrowed item she can return. She wants to repay her debt fully.

highlights.text: return what I borrowed in full

rows.jp: 「わーい」
rows.en: “Hooray.”

rows.jp: 「ただし！」
rows.en: “However!”

rows.jp: 俺の言動を遮って、強い語調で。
rows.en: She cut me off, her voice suddenly hard.

ghs.en: She intercepts my speech and conduct with strong tone.
ghs.assessment: Kiri cuts off his words and actions with a forceful tone. 'Intercepts conduct' is not idiomatic, and 'tone' requires an article.

highlights.text: intercepts my speech and conduct with strong tone

rows.jp: 「和解するつもりは、まったくありませんから」
rows.en: “I have absolutely no intention of reconciling with you.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "I have absolutely not a shred of intention to reconciliate."
ghs.assessment: The negation is misplaced after 'have,' and the normal English verb is 'reconcile,' not the rare and distracting 'reconciliate.'

highlights.text: I have absolutely not a shred of intention to reconciliate.

rows.jp: 「いいよいいよ」
rows.en: “That’s fine, that’s fine.”

rows.jp: 「それもまた人生よ」
rows.en: “Such is life.”

rows.jp: 「指示を下さい」
rows.en: “Tell me what to do.”

rows.jp: 「んじゃー、まずこれを見てくれ」
rows.en: “Then start by looking at this.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "So well, first have a look at this."

rows.jp: 図面を渡した。
rows.en: I handed her the plans.

rows.jp: キッと引き締められた顔。
rows.en: Her face snapped into a look of fierce concentration.

rows.jp: 一分後には、渋面になった―――
rows.en: Within a minute, it had soured into a grimace—

ghs.en: And after a minute, it had become a grimace---
